findings.summary: The happy path does what the card asks. Commit 55fb6a5 adds a real HTTP → PGlite → 07-A service → journal → React saved player. On that commit the controller's actual runs passed: 52/52 tests, the build, check_application_card and source-bound CUA. Together they show Confirmed appears only after acknowledgement, a lost-response retry reuses the same ID, refresh restores the exact revision, and Replay creates a separate play while keeping the old one's trials. The fix for the earlier browser finding (retried Replay now opens at the new play's introduction) is verified. However, two failure paths in the new server adapter break the card's criteria, and nothing exercises them. First, a Replay whose Start fails before anything is saved leaves an unstarted play in the server's play list. After that, every open/reload returns 403, so the player shows a false 'Access closed'. Second, a browser refresh while a save is pending blocks that play with 503 for the life of the server. The adapter only ever calls service.resume, which never finishes a pending save, and the only retry handle is lost on refresh.

findings.title: Unstarted replay entry makes every later open a false 403 Access closed
findings.problem: operate('/saved/replay') adds the new play to the server's play list (registry.set) before service.start runs. If Start throws before anything is written, the play stays in the list with no stored rows. One way this happens: the service's journal health is still 'journal_unavailable' from an earlier failed write (play-service.mjs:280 checks this before inserting). From then on, full() calls service.resume on every listed play (the history loop). For a play with no rows, the accepted service throws 'denied' (play-service.mjs:165). The whole open/reload response becomes 403, and the client wipes all confirmed content and shows 'Access closed. Play content is unavailable.' The same happens to other tabs and to fresh browser refreshes. Once the client wipes its state on 403, the replay retry handle is gone, so this lasts for the life of the server. This breaks card criteria 'denied action is not fabricated' and 'refresh resumes last confirmed state'. It also contradicts the contract doc's claim that a denial in full() means an actual WM-10 authorization denial. No test covers a Replay that fails before Start commits.
findings.fix_check: Either add a replay play to the list only after its Start has written rows, or treat an unstarted entry as history trial_count:null and not as a denial. A real HTTP test should make Replay's Start fail before commit (journal health already unavailable), then open/reload the original play and get 200 with its trials, with no 403, and then show that the Replay retry still creates exactly one new play.

findings.title: Refresh during pending save blocks the play with 503; save never completes
findings.problem: '/saved/open' for an existing play always calls service.resume. When the latest stored row is still pending, resume returns pending without retrying the journal write (play-service.mjs:328). Only a same-ID retry, or service.reconcile, completes it, and the adapter never calls reconcile. The client keeps the pending action only in memory. If the parent refreshes while the screen says Pending, which is likely, the fresh client's open returns 503 every time, even after the journal recovers. The service's journal health also stays 'journal_unavailable', so every new Start/Commit for every play in the fixture fails as well. The UI only warns that 'Unconfirmed changes may be lost'. In fact all confirmed progress for that play becomes unreachable and the whole fixture stops accepting writes. This breaks 'Refresh resumes last confirmed state' and the WM-07 requirement for known-loss/backfill handling. Neither the tests nor the CUA covered refresh while pending, so there is no evidence for this path.
findings.fix_check: When resume returns pending, have open complete the save through the accepted service (for example service.reconcile on the same server-held scope). Alternatively, show a disclosed recoverable state that does not leave the fixture permanently blocked. A real HTTP/PG/journal test should: fail the journal on an action, drop the client, restore the journal, open the play with a fresh client, and get 200 with the completed state. A later action on any play should then succeed.

findings.title: Reload after unsupported acknowledgement opens initial play, not current
findings.problem: An unsupported acknowledgement calls clear(), which sets state.play_id to null and operation to null. reload() then picks state.play_id ?? operation?.body.play_id ?? null, which is null, so it opens the server's initial preallocated play. The UI error says 'reload the original play', and the Retry button is still shown but always throws because operation is null. If the parent was on a replay or another play, they are silently moved to a different play.
findings.fix_check: Remember the selected play ID across clear('failed') for this purpose, or hide Retry and reopen the URL's play. A unit test with a malformed acknowledgement on a non-initial play should show that reload requests that same play_id.

findings.title: Retrying a failed Start/Resume read leaves the user on the introduction
findings.problem: If enterPlay's open() fails and the user presses Retry original operation, the reconciled play ID is unchanged, so the view stays on the introduction or paused recap. The user has to press Start or Resume again. This is harmless but an extra step.
findings.fix_check: After a successful retry of an entry read, move to the playing view, or document the two-step behaviour.
